Moral Foundations Theory is a framework that separates human morality into the following categories:

  - Care/Harm: related to our long evolution as mammals with attachment systems
    and an ability to feel (and dislike) the pain of others. It underlies the
    virtues of kindness, gentleness, and nurturance.

  - Loyalty/Betrayal: related to our long history as tribal creatures able to
    form shifting coalitions. It is active anytime people feel that it is "one
    for all and all for one." It underlies the virtues of patriotism and
    self-sacrifice for the group.

  - Authority/Subversion: shaped by our long primate history of hierarchical
    social interactions. It underlies virtues of leadership and followership,
    including deference to prestigious authority figures and respect for
    traditions.

  - Sanctity/Purity: shaped by the psychology of disgust and contamination. It
    underlies notions of striving to live in an elevated, less carnal, more
    noble, and more "natural" way (often present in religious narratives). This
    foundation underlies the widespread idea that the body is a temple that can
    be desecrated by immoral activities and contaminants (an idea not unique to
    religious traditions). It underlies the virtues of self-discipline,
    self-improvement, naturalness, and spirituality.

  - Equality: related to our intuitions about equal treatment and equal outcome
    for individuals.

  - Proportionality: related to our intuitions about individuals getting
    rewarded in proportion to their merit or contribution.

Labour Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (under 500 words)

Vision and funding
- “Real change” to shift wealth and power from a privileged few, end austerity and tackle the climate emergency.
- Fair tax plan: raise income tax on earnings above £80,000; reverse parts of corporation tax cuts; no VAT rise; major anti-avoidance drive; 20:1 public-sector pay ratio cap; restore public sector pay with above-inflation rises.
- Investment: £400bn National Transformation Fund (incl. £250bn Green Transformation Fund); National Investment Bank and Regional Development Banks; £150bn Social Transformation Fund for schools, hospitals, housing and care.

Green Industrial Revolution
- Target majority of UK emissions cuts by 2030; 90% of electricity and 50% of heat from low-carbon by 2030.
- 1 million climate jobs; ban fracking; windfall tax on oil firms; mass home retrofits and zero‑carbon standard for new homes; large-scale wind/solar, trial tidal and hydrogen; grid upgrades and storage.
- Public ownership of energy and water; community energy expansion.
- Transport: bring rail into public ownership; electrification, HS2 to Scotland and “Crossrail for the North”; regulate/municipalise buses (free for under‑25s where councils run routes); boost walking/cycling; end new petrol/diesel car sales by 2030; expand EV charging.

Economy, work and rights
- Real Living Wage £10+ for all 16+; ban zero-hours; day‑one rights; single “worker” status; sectoral collective bargaining.
- Reduce average full-time week to 32 hours within a decade with no loss of pay; strengthen unions; inclusive ownership funds (up to 10% employee stakes).
- Tough late-payment rules; tailored support for self‑employed.

Public services, NHS and care
- End outsourcing and PFI; presumption to insource.
- NHS: average 4.3% annual funding rise; end privatisation; free prescriptions; restore public health; invest in staff, scanners, IT and mental health (parity with physical health).
- Social care: National Care Service with free personal care, better conditions for care workers, more packages to support independent living.

Education and skills
- National Education Service: restore Sure Start (Sure Start Plus), 30 hours free pre‑school for 2–4‑year‑olds, extend paid maternity leave to 12 months.
- Schools: fair funding, max primary classes of 30, scrap SATs, Arts Premium, bring academies/free schools under democratic local control, free school meals for all primaries.
- Further/higher: lifelong learning entitlements; abolish tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; boost ESOL and adult learning.

Housing
- Build 1m+ council and social homes over a decade (150k/yr; 100k council); redefine “affordable” by income; end Right to Buy; “use it or lose it” on stalled sites.
- Private renting: rent controls, open‑ended tenancies, minimum standards/licensing, end no‑fault evictions; leasehold reform; £1bn fire safety fund; end rough sleeping in five years.

Justice, security and communities
- Rebuild neighbourhood policing; public health approach to crime; restore legal aid; reunify probation publicly; presumption against short sentences.
- Free full‑fibre broadband for all by 2030 via public ownership; Digital Rights and duty of care online.
- Strengthen local government, high streets (Post Bank, stop Crown Post Office closures), co-operatives and community wealth building.

Equality, migration and social security
- Department for Women and Equalities; close gender pay gap by 2030; stronger disability, race and LGBT+ rights.
- End the “hostile environment”; scrap 2014 Immigration Act; end indefinite detention; close Yarl’s Wood/Brook House; automatic right to remain for EU citizens.
- Scrap Universal Credit; immediate mitigations (end five‑week wait, end sanctions, scrap cap and two‑child limit); raise ESA; increase Carer’s Allowance; improve disability assessments.

Brexit and constitution
- Final‑say referendum within six months: credible leave deal (customs union, close single market alignment, rights and standards) vs remain; implement result.
- Abolish House of Lords for an elected Senate after a Constitutional Convention; votes at 16; automatic voter registration; curb dark money and lobbying.

Foreign policy and defence
- Human rights–led diplomacy; War Powers Act; recognise Palestine; suspend arms sales linked to abuses; rebuild climate diplomacy.
- Maintain NATO and 2% defence spending; renew Trident; improve forces’ pay, housing and veteran support.

TEXT_G:
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2019 – Summary (≤500 words)

Core purpose
- Put Scotland’s future in Scotland’s hands via a new independence referendum (sought through a Section 30 transfer to ensure legality). SNP open to a progressive alliance to keep the Tories out and will demand Scotland’s right to choose.

Brexit and Europe
- Scotland voted Remain; SNP backs a UK‑wide second EU referendum with Remain on the ballot and supports revoking Article 50 to prevent no‑deal.
- Whatever the UK outcome, keep the closest possible relationship with the EU, protecting the single market/customs union alignment and EU standards.

NHS and public services
- Call for UK per‑capita NHS spending to match Scotland’s, benefiting all nations and increasing Scotland’s budget via Barnett.
- Propose an NHS Protection Act to keep health services out of trade deals and protect founding principles; compensation for contaminated blood victims.
- End austerity; reverse real‑terms cuts to Scotland’s budget; invest in services and wellbeing.

Economy, tax and household costs
- Devolve more tax powers; oppose tax cuts for big business/wealthiest; crack down on avoidance.
- Cut employer National Insurance to support job creation; oppose VAT rises; reform VAT (retain exemptions; remove VAT from sanitary products, e‑publications).
- Cut energy bills via a national free switching service, clearer tariffs, and protections for credit/arrears.

Social security and equality
- Scrap the benefit freeze, the two‑child cap and rape clause; halt Universal Credit rollout and end punitive sanctions; uprate benefits at least by inflation.
- Promote dignity/respect in social security; improve terminal illness rules.
- Child poverty: support Scotland’s Scottish Child Payment; urge UK child poverty targets and a new benefit to reduce child poverty.

Pensions
- Protect the triple lock; oppose rises in state pension age; support WASPI women; restore Pension Credit for mixed‑age couples; reinstate free TV licences for over‑75s.

Migration and asylum
- Devolve immigration; oppose the hostile environment and £30k salary threshold; propose a Scottish Visa; safeguard freedom of movement.
- Reform asylum: independent decision‑maker, expand family reunion, safe legal routes, right to work, end indefinite detention; reopen Dubs scheme.

Drugs policy
- Devolve the Misuse of Drugs Act; pilot supervised drug consumption facilities to cut deaths and harm.

Work, rights and corporate reform
- Devolve employment law; lift the statutory living wage to at least the real Living Wage; end age discrimination and exploitative zero‑hours; stronger gig‑economy rights; enforce equal pay with fines.
- Improve corporate governance: worker representation on boards, fairer executive pay, climate‑risk disclosure, and tackle late payments.

Climate and energy
- Match Scotland’s world‑leading targets (75% emissions cut by 2030; net‑zero carbon by 2040; net‑zero all GHGs by 2045).
- Green Energy Deal: long‑term support for renewables (onshore wind/solar back into CfD; support tidal/floating offshore), reform transmission charges, deliver island interconnectors, expand CCS, oppose fracking and new nuclear.
- Transport: rail net‑zero by 2035; major bus priority investment; EV incentives; greener tax reform (lower VAT on efficiency/clean heat).
- Create a Net Zero Fund by ring‑fencing oil & gas receipts; expand woodland creation.

Infrastructure, regions and sectors
- Boost Scottish National Investment Bank; raise capital borrowing limits; fair share of gigabit broadband/5G; social tariffs; protect roaming.
- Fairer city/region deals; protect EU structural funds roles; support tourism (consider VAT cut).
- Rural/food: protect PGIs; secure farm funding incl. convergence uplift; strengthen the Groceries Code Adjudicator; fair fisheries control and export flow.

Democracy and rights
- Replace First Past the Post with STV; abolish House of Lords; votes at 16; extend franchise to EU citizens/residents with leave.
- Defend the Human Rights Act and ECHR; incorporate UNCRC; tackle racism/bigotry.

Security, defence and veterans
- Scrap Trident; focus on conventional defence and Scottish shipbuilding; house homeless veterans in vacant MoD homes; strengthen veterans’ rights.

Education, families and consumers
- Expand early learning and childcare; close the attainment gap; free higher education.
- Extend parental leave/pay and protections; neonatal leave.
- Protect access to cash and post offices; curb high‑cost credit and ticket touting; regulate online harms with a statutory duty of care and independent regulator.

Overall: independence within Europe, escape Brexit, protect public services and the NHS, end austerity, tackle poverty and the climate emergency, and modernise democracy.
